You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
### Diagnosis

The failing test `testNullRecordSeparatorCsv106` in `CSVFormatTest` creates a CSV format with a specific configuration and then formats two values "A" and "B" using `CSVFormat.format`. The test expects the formatted string to be "A;B" without any appended "null" value at the end. However, the actual output includes "A;Bnull".

Upon inspecting the source code, we can see that the `CSVFormat.format` method delegates the formatting to `CSVPrinter.printRecord` method, which iterates over the provided values and prints each one followed by a delimiter. The final call in this loop is to `CSVPrinter.println`, which appends a newline character at the end of the line.

The issue in this case is likely due to the absence of a record terminator after the last value. When the `CSVPrinter.printRecord` method finishes printing the values, it appends a newline character. Because there is no record terminator after the last value "B", the newline character gets appended directly after "B", resulting in the unexpected output "A;Bnull".

### Proposed Fix
- `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.printRecord(java.lang.Object...)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
